en: Contrary to the old 7,107 figure, the Philippines actually consists of 7,641 islands based on a 2016 mapping survey.
Many think Mount Apo is in Davao City, but it is actually located across Davao del Sur and Cotabato.
The Cagayan River, rather than the shorter Pasig River, is the longest river in the Philippines at 505 kilometers.
Although Laguna de Bay is the largest, Lake Taal is actually the deepest lake in the Philippines.
People assume Mayon Volcano is dormant due to its perfect shape, but it is highly active with over fifty eruptions.
Baguio City is cold because of its high elevation of 1,500 meters, not because it is near the ocean.
Many think Palawan is like the rest of the country, but it is geologically part of the Asian continental shelf.
The Tubbataha Reefs are not on the Palawan mainland, but are actually located in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows into the South China Sea, not the Pacific Ocean as some mistakenly believe.
Mount Pinatubo was never the highest mountain, as Mount Apo has always been the highest peak in the Philippines.
The Chocolate Hills are not made of chocolate soil, but are marine limestone formations that turn brown in the dry season.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is not a single province, but a region composed of six distinct provinces.
